column1: # THE FLAT EXPERIMENT, EXPERIMENTALIST VERSION (2026-11-12; the user: "it means nothing if we gave ptyco an exact probe ... what's interesting is
# that we gave it a realistic set of parameters and it FIT TO THE PHASE"). gflat's lone atom could not fit a released probe: from the crystal
# search's misses the probe overlap went 0.40 -> 0.44 and every kernel broke, the perfect 80 mrad probe's too. A lone atom in vacuum gives the
# solver almost nothing to fit a probe against; an experimentalist fits on a specimen. So the same lines on the campaign's kernel geometry:
# a grid of Pb atoms on one plane, 3 A apart, 20 A scan at 0.5 A, the kernel averaged over its atoms.
#   PROBE_UPDATE=1 GROUPING="32;16" bash runs/zb_submit.sh runs/ggrid.tsv          (from the search's misses; RTAG _pu)
#   GROUPING="32;16" bash runs/zb_submit.sh runs/ggrid.tsv                         (the reference, true probe fixed; after the sims)
# 30 and 40 mrad in a 40 A box at 1 A slices (NL 40), 60 and 80 in the campaign's 27.5 A grid box (NL 28, 0.98 A). flat30 in a 45 A window.
